context: You are a member of a local community library. You received an email from the head librarian.

paragraphs: I hope this message finds you well. I regret to inform you that the library will be closed for two weeks starting next Friday for renovations and upgrades to our facilities. We aim to enhance your reading experience.
In the meantime, we would love to hear your suggestions on what new programs or services we could offer upon reopening. Your input is invaluable to us.

task11: Write a letter to your friend, who is also a member of the library. Write about your feelings and what you think the library management should do about the situation.
task12: Write a letter to the head librarian. Write about your feelings and what you think the library management should do about the situation.
part2_question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of online learning compared to traditional classroom learning?

task11: Did you get the email? The library is closing for two weeks for renovations. I'm really disappointed, because I have just started a new series. I think they should set up a small shelf in the community hall so that members can still borrow books. What do you think?
task12: Thank you for letting us know about the upcoming renovations. I understand that the building needs to be upgraded, but I must admit that I feel disappointed, because the library is an important part of my week and two weeks is a long time without it.

I would like to suggest a few things. Firstly, it would help enormously if members could borrow extra books just before the closure. Secondly, a temporary collection in the community hall would keep the service running for readers who cannot afford to buy books.
Finally, when the library reopens, I would love to see more e-books and audiobooks, as well as evening workshops or author talks. Clear updates about the reopening date would also be very welcome.
part2: That is a very relevant question, and having studied in both ways, I can see clear advantages and disadvantages.

The biggest advantage of online learning is flexibility. You can open the materials whenever your schedule allows, which is invaluable if you are working or looking after a family. You can also repeat a difficult explanation as many times as you need, which is impossible in a live class. In addition, the range of resources available online, from interactive exercises to huge digital libraries, is far wider than any single classroom can offer.

On the other hand, a traditional classroom offers a social dynamic that is hard to reproduce on a screen. Face-to-face contact with the teacher and the other students produces immediate feedback and spontaneous discussion, and this really does increase both understanding and motivation. Group activities in a real room fix new vocabulary in your memory in a way that breakout rooms rarely do, and studying alone online can feel isolating.
Overall, I believe the best solution is a blended approach that combines the convenience of online resources with the human contact of the classroom.
